about: Universal Credit monthly amounts and earnings rules for tools/build-universal-credit-pages.js, each quoted from GOV.UK and DWP's benefit and pension rates. The amounts change each April.

sources.title: Universal Credit: how your wages affect your payments
Universal Credit if you have children

standard.quote: If you’re single and under 25 £338.58 If you’re single and 25 or over £424.90 If you live with your partner and you’re both under 25 £528.34 (for you both) If you live with your partner and either of you are 25 or over £666.97 (for you both)

child.quote: You’ll get £303.94 a month for each child that lives with you. If your first child was born before 6 April 2017, you’ll get an extra £47.94 a month for that child.

twoChildLimit.quote: The 2-child limit ended on 6 April 2026 Universal Credit now pays the extra amount for every child, no matter how many children you have.

disabledChild.quote: £164.79 - the lower amount £514.71 - the higher amount

health.quote: If you have a severe health condition or disability that’s unlikely to change or you are nearing the end of your life £429.80 If your health condition or disability is assessed as less severe or your condition may improve over time £217.26 There are different rules if you reported a health condition before 6 April 2026

healthRates.quote: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity amount | 423.27 | 217.26 | Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity amount (Pre-2026 claimant, severe conditions criteria claimant or claimant who is terminally ill) | 423.27 | 429.80

carer.quote: You’ll get an extra monthly amount of £209.34. If you live with your partner and you both care for the same person, you’ll only get one extra monthly amount.

carerNotWithHealth.quote: If you are getting an extra amount because you have limited capability for work and work related activity (LCWRA), you cannot also get the carer’s element.

childcare.quote: You can claim back up to 85% of your childcare costs if you’re working. If you live with your partner both of you need to be working, unless one of you is unable to work due to a disability or health condition.

childcareMax.quote: The most you can get each month is: £1,071.09 for one child £1,836.16 for 2 or more children

taper.quote: For every £1 you earn from working, your Universal Credit payment goes down by 55p. Your income will be your wages plus your new Universal Credit payment.

workAllowanceWho.quote: You can earn a certain amount before your Universal Credit starts to be reduced if you or your partner are either: responsible for a child or young person living with a disability or health condition that affects your ability to work

workAllowanceLower.quote: You can earn up to £427 a month before your payment starts to reduce if either: you get help with housing costs through Universal Credit you live in temporary accommodation arranged by your council because you’re homeless

workAllowanceHigher.quote: If neither of these circumstances apply to you, you can earn up to £710 a month before your payment starts to reduce.

noHoursLimit.quote: There’s no limit to how many hours you can work and still get Universal Credit.

takeHome.quote: A workplace pension run by your employer should already be taken into account, as Universal Credit is based on your net take-home pay.

statutoryPay.quote: Any statutory pay you receive is treated as earnings, in the same way as your regular wages.

otherBenefits.quote: Your Universal Credit payment will be reduced by an amount equal to the other benefit’s payment.

capital.quote: If you have over £6,000 in money, savings and investments, your payment will be reduced by £4.35 for every £250 you have between £6,000 and £16,000. Another £4.35 is taken off for any remaining amount that is not a complete £250.

capitalLimit.quote: have £16,000 or less in money, savings and investments

benefitCapEarnings.quote: get Universal Credit and you and your partner earn £881 or more a month combined, after tax and National Insurance contributions

benefitCapAmounts.quote: Benefit cap outside Greater London Per week Per month If you’re in a couple £423.46 £1,835 If you’re a single parent and your children live with you £423.46 £1,835 If you’re a single adult £283.71 £1,229.42 Benefit cap inside Greater London Per week Per month If you’re in a couple £486.98 £2,110.25 If you’re a single parent and your children live with you £486.98 £2,110.25 If you’re a single adult £326.29 £1,413.92
